summary: A 1909 crow's nest at Hopi Point, Grand Canyon, became a 1927 steel tower; a 1953 remodel lowered it to 24 ft, and it has been inactive since at least 2009.

facts.design: 12 x 12 ft cab on a 24 ft steel tower after the 1953 remodel

visit.trail_note: Reached on foot by the walking trail from Grand Canyon Village; the sources do not say whether the tower itself may be climbed

events.note: Fire lookout stationed at the Hopi Tower; visitors registered at the tower that season
A fire lookout accepted a position at Hopi station (July 1921 item)
National Park Service replaced the crow's nest with a 40 ft steel tower
Cab enlarged to 12 x 12 ft and tower lowered to 24 ft during a remodel
Park Service said all four Grand Canyon lookout towers on the register were inactive

evidence.supports: 1953 remodel with 12 x 12 cab; tower lowered to 24 ft
evidence.quote: The lookout was remodeled in 1953 with this 12'x12' cab and the tower lowered to 24'.

evidence.supports: no longer used for fire detection
evidence.quote: The lookout is no longer used for fire detection.

evidence.supports: Forest Service built a tree-top crow's nest in 1909 to scout for forest fires
evidence.quote: As early as 1909, the Forest Service built a tree-top crow’s nest at Hopi Point in order to scout for forest fires

evidence.supports: 1927 NPS replaced with a 40 foot steel tower; lowered to 24 feet in 1953 when remodeled
evidence.quote: In 1927 the National Park Service replaced this with a 40 foot steel tower, which was lowered to 24 feet in 1953 when the top was remodeled.

corrections.proposed: built 1909 (Forest Service crow's nest); replaced 1927 (40 ft steel tower); modified 1953 (remodel, tower lowered to 24 ft)
corrections.why: The 1953 work was a remodel of a tower that dated from 1927. The first lookout on the site was a 1909 crow's nest, so 1953 is not the build year.

sources.title: Hopi Point - Nature, Culture and History at the Grand Canyon
Four Grand Canyon National Park Lookout Towers have been listed on the National Historic Lookout Register

notes_for_editor: The record's built 1953 comes from the NHLR Built field, but the NHLR text and the grcahistory page both describe 1953 as a remodel of the 1927 tower; the 1909 crow's nest is the first lookout. Current access to the tower is not in any source read, so the visit fact is limited to the public trail. Unstaffed as of 2009 is inferred from the NHLR statement that the tower is no longer used for fire detection and the 2009 NPS statement that the towers are inactive; no current staffing source was found. The FFLA and NHLR coordinates differ by about 538 m (record conflict); I did not check which is right. The NHLR photo is already in the record; no new photos checked.
